Repeats the upward movement for Joseph and those accompanying him, rather than only saying they accompanied him.
“They left” retains the active verb rather than “were left.”
Calls the gathering a “camp” or company rather than a “procession.”
Calls the lament great and very heavy, retaining the weight image rather than describing loud wailing.
Calls this “heavy mourning,” rather than a “solemn ceremony of mourning.”
Retains “his sons,” without explicitly naming Jacob.

Retains the age expression “a son of a hundred and ten years.” The embalming is active, but being placed in the coffin is passive, rather than both actions having an active plural subject.
